did_you_know.text: The phrase strange fire can mean foreign fire or fire that was not permitted. The verse does not explain exactly what was wrong with it; it stresses that God had not commanded it.
The verb vayidom means became silent or fell quiet. The Torah describes Aaron’s response to the tragedy in a single word, without giving him a speech or explanation.

Tearing clothes and letting the hair hang loose were common mourning practices in the ancient world. Here the priests are forbidden to mourn in that way while serving, while the rest of the people are told to grieve.
The word shekhar refers to an intoxicating drink, not only to wine. The prohibition therefore includes wine as well as other strong or fermented drinks.
The verse presents two different distinctions: holy versus ordinary, and impure versus pure. Impure does not necessarily mean morally bad; it refers to a particular ritual status.

The waved breast and raised thigh were given not only to the priests but also to their family members, including their daughters. This shows that the priest’s household shared in certain sacred foods.

Aaron explains why he did not eat the sin offering that day, and Moses accepts his explanation. The ending suggests that unusual circumstances may call for judgment, not merely mechanical obedience to a rule.
